title: antislop-sampler (README)
technique: Decoding-time backtracking: when a listed word/phrase appears, back up and down-weight the tokens that produced it; per-entry multipliers, regex bans, adjustment_strength 0-100+
result: No quality or benchmark numbers on the page. Phrase-level match avoids penalising shared first tokens (e.g. 'El' in 'Elara').
models: Any local model exposing raw logits (Transformers, koboldcpp)
cost_or_caveat: Needs logit access, so not usable on hosted Claude/GPT APIs; README says research-grade, not optimised, no concurrency, no streaming with regex bans

title: Antislop (Paech et al., ICLR 2026)
technique: Antislop sampler (backtracking) and FTPO (Final Token Preference Optimization, fine-tune)
result: Sampler suppresses 8,000+ patterns while maintaining quality; plain token banning becomes unusable at about 2,000. FTPO about 90% slop reduction while maintaining or improving GSM8K, MMLU and creative-writing evals. DPO suppresses slop less and degrades writing quality and lexical diversity. Some slop patterns appear >1,000x more often in LLM than human text.
models: Not stated in the abstract I read
cost_or_caveat: Abstract only; per-model numbers not read. Needs open weights (FTPO) or logits (sampler)

title: slop-score
technique: Slop metric definition used by EQ-Bench
result: Composite: 60% slop words, 25% not-X-but-Y patterns (10 + 35 regexes), 15% slop trigrams; lists built by comparing AI text with human baselines. 150 creative + 150 essay outputs per model.
cost_or_caveat: No per-model scores on the page. Usable as a local linter for our own output (not-X-but-Y detector especially)

title: EQ-Bench Creative Writing v3
technique: Leaderboard with Elo and Slop columns
result: Fetched page had an empty table, so no per-model slop scores obtained. Describes Slop as frequency of overused words/phrases against a master list; v3 is 32 prompts x 3 iterations, LLM-judged rubric + pairwise Elo.
cost_or_caveat: Could not read leaderboard rows. Aggregator figures (slop 11.14, Gemma 2 9B 67.68) were seen only in snippets, with unknown dates and scales; not recorded as results

title: Hemingway-bench (Surge AI)
technique: Expert-human blind pairwise comparison of models on writing
result: 5,000+ blind comparisons by professional writers. Top three: Gemini 3 Flash, Gemini 3 Pro, Claude Opus 4.5. Judges found Opus 4.5 the most natural voice, least like it was trying to impress. GPT-5.2 API weak on creative work. Surge reports EQ-Bench autograder agreed with its experts as little as 43% and favoured an overwritten, metaphor-packed story.
models: Gemini 3 Flash/Pro, Claude Opus 4.5, GPT-5.2, Qwen3, Grok, Kimi K2, Llama 4 Maverick, Nova
cost_or_caveat: Vendor-run; Elo values were in an image. Search snippet (not fetched from the source) gave Elo: Gemini 3.1 Pro 1093, Gemini 3 Flash 1088, Gemini 3 Pro 1082, Claude Opus 4.6 1064, Opus 4.5 1047, Sonnet 4.6 1032, GPT-5.2 Chat 1029, GPT-5.4 1022, GPT-5.2 990

title: Min-p, Max Exaggeration (Schaeffer et al.)
technique: Re-analysis of min-p sampling (Nguyen et al. 2407.01082)
result: Reanalysis found min-p did not outperform baselines in quality, diversity, or the trade-off; original human-eval data omitted and wrong tests used; a new human eval by the original authors also showed no improvement; benchmarks show no win once hyperparameter count is controlled.
models: Models from the original min-p study
cost_or_caveat: Original paper claimed gains at high temperature (AlpacaEval Creative Writing). Net: sampler tweaks are not an established lever for diversity or slop. Neither paper targets slop phrases

title: How Well Do LLMs Imitate Human Writing Style?
technique: Zero-shot vs one-shot vs few-shot vs text-completion prompting, scored by an authorship verifier
result: Style-match accuracy: zero-shot 3.1-6.9%; one-shot 67.6-94.7%; few-shot 91-100%; text completion 96.9-100%. Perplexity: human essays 29.5, LLM outputs about 15-16.
cost_or_caveat: Measures matching a style per a verifier (essays), not slop or fiction quality; the text-completion framing (continue a document) did best, a cheap trick for exemplars

title: Catch Me If You Can? Not Yet
technique: Few-shot exemplars (5 samples + content summary) of everyday authors; 2-10 demonstrations
result: GPT-4o top-5 authorship attribution 5-shot vs 0-shot: Enron 59.65 vs 28.62, Blog 39.39 vs 17.22, Reddit 27.12 vs 18.77, CCAT50 86.64 vs 83.88. 2 to 10 examples: very little further effect. GPTZero called most outputs AI (often <20% human; GPT-4o near zero; Gemini-2.0-Flash 54.25% human on Enron 5-shot). Adding a snippet of the author's own text gave the biggest human-likeness boost.
models: GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, Gemini-2.0-Flash, Gemma-3-27B, DeepSeek-V3, Llama-4-Maverick
cost_or_caveat: Informal writing (blogs, forums) stays weak; authors suspect GPTZero is biased toward GPT-style text, so cross-family gaps are shaky

title: Base Models Look Human To AI Detectors (CMU, May 2026)
technique: Base-model generation, and Humanization by Iterative Paraphrasing (HIP) with a fine-tuned base-model paraphraser
result: GPTZero and Pangram judge base-model text overwhelmingly human, instruction-tuned text not. HIP improves detector human-likeness across Llama-3 and Qwen-3, 0.6B-70B; iterative paraphrasing raises human probability with gradual loss of semantic fidelity.
cost_or_caveat: Measures detector scores, not reader-perceived quality; I read only summaries. Suggests the tics come from instruction tuning, so a base-model draft or edit pass is the lever, but needs open weights

title: DAMAGE: Detecting Adversarially Modified AI Generated Text (Pangram)
result: Many existing detectors fail on humanized text; paper built a detector robust to it. No finding that humanizers improve prose quality.
cost_or_caveat: Detector-evasion framing; qualitative faithfulness check only. Null for 'humanizers fix slop': evidence is about evading detectors, not reader-facing quality

title: LLM Output Diversity is Everything, Everywhere, All at Once; and Moon et al. homogenization study (via search summary)
technique: Prompt and parameter changes (persona, temperature) to restore diversity
result: Summary: human essays added more new ideas than GPT-4 essays (2,200 admissions essays), a gap that persisted despite prompt and parameter modifications; briefs/keywords raise novelty of single ideas but outputs stay in a shared semantic space.
cost_or_caveat: Second-hand summary from a search result; not fetched. Consistent with the existing llm-writing.md finding that personas did not help

title: Null result
technique: Multi-step draft-then-edit and negative instructions ('avoid X')
result: Found no study measuring a draft/critique/rewrite pipeline or a negative-instruction list against a slop metric. Not a finding that they fail; I did not find a measurement.
cost_or_caveat: Two searches only; Antislop paper's full text (may compare prompt-based banning) was not read
